item.title: Why startups fail: test the assumptions
item.description: The often-repeated “90%” headline is not a universal three-year failure rate. Definitions of startups, closure and failure differ. This article focuses on questions you can investigate instead of treating a headline as your personal odds.

item.title: How much money does a startup need?
item.description: There is no universal startup budget. This is a planning exercise: replace every example with quotations, expenses and demand evidence for your situation.

item.title: Customer acquisition cost: formulas and examples
item.description: Channel costs vary with audience, market, offer and measurement window. The examples here are hypothetical arithmetic, not verified 2026 market benchmarks.

item.title: Churn: measure retention and test improvements
item.description: Define your cohort and time window before comparing retention. Customer churn and revenue churn answer different questions. No single monthly percentage is good for every business.
